annotations.title: Find Contractors Named in Arms Notices

description: Look up a contractor family in the Arms Sales Register by a substring of its reviewed family name or of a company string as the notices print it. Returns up to 5 families, each with the companies the family includes and the strings as printed; the notices naming it by year delivered and by its leading buyers; the estimated value of the notices naming it (shared, never split), with the notices naming it alone, among the companies a competition will choose from, and since January 20, 2025; the joint ventures it is a parent of; and the side columns, each from its own record: its connected PAC's contributions to federal candidates' committees and its contributions to all committees, by FEC cycle (FEC bulk files; no committee it gave to, candidate or party is named), its 2025 lobbying reports (lda.gov; in-house expenses and outside firms' income are each the report's total for all issues and are never added together), the 2025 inaugural committee's report and the reviewed super PAC donors, with the caption. An empty column is a search result, not a fact about the company. Each row is a proposed sale notified to Congress, and its value is the estimated value the notice prints: never a price, a signed case, a contract or a payment. A company appears only as a notice names it, resolved to the register's reviewed family table: the value of the notices naming a family is shared, never split between the companies a notice names, never added across families and never described as company revenue. The estimated value notified, FARA money, connected-PAC money, lobbying amounts and the inaugural and super PAC records are separate records, shown side by side: never added together and never put in date sequence with a notice. Every answer carries the register's question note: these are proposed sales the Defense Department notified to Congress, as printed in the Federal Register; a notification is not a completed sale, and the records do not show why any sale was proposed or whether it went ahead. Every answer also carries the side-by-side caption, the as-of date, the date the Federal Register copies are printed through, each file's date, the source page on morvs.ai and the licence. Where FEC figures appear, the answer quotes the FEC's restriction on the sale or use of individual contributor information (52 U.S.C. 30111(a)(4)). Institutions only: no official, signer, lobbyist, treasurer, candidate or member of Congress is named, and single-person firms are withheld and appear only as counts. A name that matches only a withheld string answers exactly like a name that matches nothing. No party label is given and no buyer government is characterised.

name.description: Required case-insensitive substring of a reviewed contractor family name or of a company string as the notices print it; at most 80 characters.
